title: Capability-announce dispatch returns 2.04 when CapabilityTable::insert refuses (Python resource returns 5.03)
description: Found by worker-1's audit of the landed 7nnl.3 dispatch (kimi-k3 verification pass, the 'real behavioral divergence from the mirrored Python resource'). rust/lichen-gateway/src/resources.rs:1746 ignores the bool returned by CapabilityTable::insert: a non-egress insert refused by the 25% egress reservation (capability.rs, table full with reserved entries protected) is silently dropped while the announcer still gets 2.04 Changed - a false-success claim that the capability was cached. The mirrored Python resource (python/.../capability_announce.py record path) returns 5.03 Service Unavailable on refusal. Fix: propagate the insert result - refuse -> 5.03 (spec-aligned with the Python resource), keep 2.04 only when the entry actually landed; then add the dispatch-level Rust test mirrors the reviewer flagged as missing vs the python resource cases: expired -> 4.03, kid/IID mismatch -> 4.03, seq-regression-then-recovery (5 reject -> 6 accept), table-full -> 5.03. Note: missing-peer-pubkey divergence (Rust 4.01 vs Python 4.03) is unreachable in practice (pre-dispatch trust-store gate) - leave as is. Also LICHEN_EGRESS updates refresh in place so the egress-reserved partition never refuses an egress refresh; the refusal path is non-egress inserts only.
close_reason: Fixed: handle_post_capability_announce now propagates CapabilityTable::insert's bool - a refused insert responds 5.03 Service Unavailable (new CoapResponse::service_unavailable, 0xA3) instead of the false 2.04, matching the mirrored Python resource (record() False -> SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE); 2.04 is returned only when the entry actually landed. New dispatch-level test capability_announce_rejects_recover_and_table_full_is_503 covers the reviewer-flagged missing mirrors: expired -> 4.03; seq regression then recovery (5 accept -> 4 reject 4.03 with cached_seq preserved at 5 -> 6 accept 2.04); the true Rust refusal path (fill all 256 slots with egress entries, new non-egress announcer via a second keypair -> insert false -> 5.03, cached_seq stays None). IMPORTANT REFINEMENT of the original finding: the reviewer's 'regular-partition-full -> refusal' premise was wrong for Rust - CapabilityTable::insert EVICTS the LRU non-egress entry and admits in that case (landed, unit-tested design); insert() returns false only when the table is at 256 AND no non-egress victim exists, or on an egress-clearing refresh with regular full. The genuine cross-stack divergence (Python refuses non-egress at the regular-tail limit, Rust evicts-and-admits) is filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-oev1 for the policy decision. The handler fix is correct under EITHER policy (never claim success without caching). Verification: cargo test -p lichen-gateway 250 lib passed incl. the new test (end_to_end red = known ljgs gate); fmt + clippy clean. Reviewer pass 1 (kimi-k3) TIMED OUT at 10min - all three lenses self-run: correctness (0xA3=5.03 per RFC 7252; seq-gate arithmetic; 256-fill eviction boundary walked; refusal condition re-derived from capability.rs insert()), security (5.03 empty payload, no claim material; success/refusal distinguishable by design per Python parity), edge (egress-refresh path unaffected, u32::try_from far_future safe, no existing test broke). Commits: 6653ff8547 (labeled) + 470fabec62 (sync).
